Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: ProtoFusion: Protocol-Guided Prompt Refinement for Generative Infrared and Visible Image Fusion
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Infrared and visible image fusion integrates complementary information from both modalities to provide a more comprehensive representation of the scene. We propose ProtoFusion, a protocol-guided generative framework for infrared and visible image fusion. Instead of relying on fixed fusion operators, hand-crafted objectives, or manually specified one-shot prompts, ProtoFusion formulates fusion as protocol-constrained generation. It represents fusion intent with a structured protocol, consisting of environment state cards, grounding principles, and a style profile, which explicitly specifies which evidence should be preserved or suppressed and which properties the fused result should satisfy. To optimize this protocol, we introduce protocol-guided prompt refinement, a closed-loop learning framework that iteratively performs generation, evaluation, and revision under multimodal evidence. Once learned, the optimized protocol is fixed at inference time and directly guides fusion generation. To address residual source inconsistencies, we further incorporate structured belief construction, which organizes modality reliability, scene evidence, and cross-modal conflicts into a structured representation for conservative correction after generation. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks show that ProtoFusion improves quantitative performance, achieves favorable results in aesthetic evaluation, and produces visually coherent fusion outputs. Project Page: {https://erfect2020.github.io/ProtoFusion/}.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: MaskSense: Confronting the Visual Exploration Trap in Masked Image Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has shown strong potential for aligning generative models with human intent, but adapting RL to masked generative models (MGMs) remains largely underexplored. Existing approaches that directly adapt Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to MGMs leave a foundational conflict unaddressed: MGMs' exploitative decoding nature is inherently at odds with the exploratory diversity that GRPO presupposes. In this work, we reveal a structural decoding bias termed the visual exploration trap: confidence-based sampling trades the exploration of diverse subject realizations for the greedy resolution of low-uncertainty background regions, causing premature collapse of the generative exploration space and starving GRPO of the rollout diversity it depends on. To this end, we propose MaskSense, a novel RL framework for MGMs that confronts the visual exploration trap at both the sampling and optimization stages. Specifically, we introduce a semantic anchored routing sampling mechanism that leverages semantic priors to preserve high-entropy subject token exploration while amplifying intra-group reward variance through exploratory-exploitative routing to yield more discriminative advantage estimates. Furthermore, we design a global entropy transition anchoring strategy to identify the most consequential decoding steps and concentrate gradient updates on them. Extensive experiments on multiple text-to-image benchmarks demonstrate that MaskSense substantially improves upon the base model, with GenEval accuracy improving from 54% to 86% and HPS from 28.89 to 36.39, achieving state-of-the-art performance.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. Project Page: https://yawen-shao.github.io/MaskSense/

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Performance evaluation of super-resolution techniques for characterization and phenotyping of commodity crops using multispectral imagery
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Multispectral imagery provides spectral information beyond the visible range for vegetation monitoring, but it typically suffers from limited spatial resolution, which can obscure fine crop structures and affect vegetation-index (VI) estimates.} This study evaluates whether single-image super-resolution (SISR) methods developed for red, green, and blue (RGB) imagery can enhance the spatial resolution of red, green, and near-infrared (RGN) crop images while preserving spectral fidelity. Eight pretrained methods are applied directly to RGN images without fine-tuning: bicubic and nearest-neighbor interpolation, Real-ESRGAN, HAT, HiT-SR, SRFormer, ResShift, and StableSR. Reconstruction at $4\times$ and $16\times$ is evaluated for whole images and manually segmented leaf regions. Reconstruction quality is assessed using mean absolute error (MAE), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index (SSIM), spectral angle mapper (SAM), and erreur relative globale adimensionnelle de synthèse (ERGAS). Eight VIs, computed from reference and super-resolved images, are evaluated using MAE, PSNR, and SSIM. Transformer-based methods \modification{significantly} outperform GAN- and diffusion-based approaches in both evaluation settings \modification{($p < 0.001$)}, with \modification{HAT, HiT-SR, and SRFormer forming the highest-performing statistical tier}. These findings indicate that RGB-trained SISR can enhance spatial detail in RGN crop imagery while maintaining spectral consistency and VI reliability for high-resolution crop phenotyping.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Solv3R: 3D Looped Transformer as a Multi-view Solver
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Classical structure-from-motion reconstruction proceeds iteratively, refining camera poses and scene geometry from a current estimate. This allows maps to easily expand without recomputing already computed views, or geometry estimates to improve as more observations are provided. Most geometric foundation models, however, predict entire geometry in a single forward pass or update a recurrent state as frames arrive sequentially, making this expansion and refinement non-trivial. We introduce Solv3R, a looped transformer that learns to continue solving multi-view geometry from its current state. Importantly, its update operator is independent of the iteration count, allowing previously refined and newly introduced views to be jointly updated regardless of how ``solved'' they are. We train the operator to preserve accurate reconstructions under continued iteration and correct inaccurate states, enabling refinement of fixed image collections and integration of new observations. Representations of solved views can also be cached once and reused as geometric context across iterations, enabling compact and efficient key-value caching. We analyze the solver dynamics and compare it with the state-of-the-art, demonstrating that a single learned solver supports offline reconstruction, incremental reconstruction, relocalization, and streaming without task-specific training or modules. The code and models will be made publicly available at https://ubc-vision.github.io/solv3r/.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Task Adaptation Through Guidance in Frozen Feature Upsampling
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Adapting features before upsampling can improve dense prediction, but the gains may arise from changes in feature values, spatial aggregation, or both. We investigate this ambiguity by comparing matched residual adapters before and after a frozen JAFAR upsampler under a shared parent. We construct a readout-null intervention that preserves a frozen linear classifier's coarse logits while allowing spatial attention weights to adapt. Guidance/value exchanges on trained models and retrained fixed-guidance controls test the utility of this adaptation route. In three-seed experiments on PASCAL Visual Object Classes (VOC) and Cityscapes, adaptation before upsampling improves mean intersection over union (mIoU) by 0.807 and 1.413 percentage points, respectively, over adaptation after upsampling. Across both datasets and the JAFAR and AnyUp upsamplers, readout-null adaptation produces mean gains of 1.379-1.987 points over the corresponding frozen linear baselines. Retrained controls further support the benefit of adaptive spatial guidance. These findings explain how dense predictions can improve despite unchanged coarse classifier outputs and identify spatial guidance as a useful target when adapting frozen feature upsampling systems.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Scaling Action-Free Video Latent Prediction for Transferable Representations in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: End-to-end autonomous driving policies require effective visual representations that capture both spatial scene structure and temporal dynamics. Video latent prediction has emerged as an effective paradigm for learning spatiotemporal visual representations, yet it remains unclear whether scaling this objective with action-free driving videos can yield representations that benefit end-to-end planning. We study action-free video latent prediction as a scalable pretraining objective and introduce ScaleDrive, a driving-oriented framework pretrained exclusively on large-scale internet open-world driving videos, without action annotations or benchmark-specific data. We keep the pretrained video encoder frozen during downstream end-to-end planning training to isolate the transferability of representations learned from internet driving videos. Ego-motion and depth probes show that scaling action-free video pretraining progressively strengthens the temporal and geometric information encoded in the frozen representation. We systematically study the visual representation transfer across different end-to-end driving policies and closed-loop benchmarks, where ScaleDrive consistently improves downstream performance and demonstrates that scaling action-free video latent prediction yields representations that generalize across both planning policy architectures and evaluation scenarios and protocols.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Aerial Content-Aware Sample-Adaptive Classifier for Urban Photogrammetric Point Cloud Segmentation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Urban photogrammetric point clouds are commonly processed as local 3D patches, limiting the context available for distinguishing geometrically similar categories. Orthographic projection of the same data yields a co-registered digital orthophoto map (DOM)/RGB-D representation that supports efficient large-context modeling but compresses vertical geometry. Existing projection--point methods mainly fuse these two representations at the feature level while retaining a classifier shared across all samples. We present the Aerial Content-Aware Sample-Adaptive Classifier (ACASAC), which complements feature fusion with decision-level adaptation. A point-aligned aerial region bridges the full aerial crop and local 3D patch. ACASAC models scene-to-local variation within the projection and the representation discrepancy between aligned 2D and 3D supports, then transfers both relations to refine the local point class representation. The refined representation, scene-level aerial context, and fixed fused-head prior jointly form a classifier for the current sample. ACASAC improves the fixed dual-representation head by 2.1 and 2.7 mIoU points on SensatUrban and UrbanBIS, respectively, and by 2.1--2.3 points across four tested encoder combinations.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Towards Zero-Shot Transfer Across Embodiments For Driving VLAs
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) have shown strong potential in autonomous driving by leveraging multimodal pretraining for instruction following, visual reasoning, and scene-level generalization. In robotic manipulation, scaling VLA fine-tuning across multiple robot setups--especially when unifying representations across embodiments--has been shown to improve in-dataset performance and cross-embodiment generalization; in autonomous driving, however, VLAs remain largely trained on individual datasets and are rarely evaluated for zero-shot transfer to unseen datasets and camera rigs; furthermore naively adding more datasets to the training data does not necessarily lead to better performance within seen embodiments. To address these problems, we study multi-dataset training for the driving task and BEV-Forcing, an auxiliary objective that transfers ground-plane object-layout information from a specialized Bird's-Eye-View model into the VLA backbone. By encouraging the model to represent object position through a shared BEV spatial interface, we show that an auxiliary task such as BEV-Forcing can improve both in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance when training on a small number of camera rigs. As the number of training embodiments increases, however, the benefits of the auxiliary task are reduced; we present this as evidence that new techniques in the literature may see their benefits diminish when simply scaling up training diversity, which motivates presenting results taking into account data scaling.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: FDSG: Forecasting Dynamic Scene Graphs
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Dynamic scene graph generation extends scene graph generation from images to videos by modeling entity relationships and their temporal evolution. However, existing methods either generate scene graphs from observed frames without explicitly modeling temporal dynamics or predict only relationships while assuming static entity labels and locations. These limitations hinder effective extrapolation of both entity and relationship dynamics, restricting video scene understanding. We propose Forecasting Dynamic Scene Graphs (FDSG), a novel framework that predicts future entity labels, bounding boxes, and relationships, for unobserved frames while also generating scene graphs for observed frames. Our scene graph forecast module leverages query decomposition and neural stochastic differential equations to model entity and relationship dynamics. A temporal aggregation module further refines predictions by integrating observed and forecasted information via cross-attention. To benchmark FDSG, we introduce Scene Graph Forecasting, a new task for full future scene graph prediction. Extensive experiments on Action Genome and VidOR show that FDSG outperforms state-of-the-art methods on dynamic scene graph generation, scene graph anticipation, and scene graph forecasting. Codes will be released upon publication.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Disen-Forcing: Disentangling Semantic Anchoring from Motion for Autoregressive Video Diffusion
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Autoregressive video diffusion models (AR-VDMs) enable real-time, long-horizon video generation but degrade rapidly once the inference horizon outruns the training horizon, due to compounding exposure bias. To stabilize long rollouts, recent methods heuristically adopt frame sink, keeping initial frames as a persistent model context, inspired by attention sinks in LLMs. We revisit this design and find that the mechanism by which initial frames stabilize long-range consistency in AR-VDMs is not an LLM-style attention sink; instead, long-range consistency is anchored through a sparse subset of attention heads, while the majority of heads predominantly capture local temporal dynamics. This observation reveals an over-conditioning pathology in existing frame-sink strategies: by universally exposing every head to the pinned initial-frame context, the model becomes prone to collapsing motion toward the low-dynamic modes of the teacher during model distillation. We propose Disen-Forcing, a distillation-time plug-in for AR-VDMs that disentangles and reinforces this head specialization through disentangled context routing and motion-disentangling regularization. On long-horizon video generation benchmarks, Disen-Forcing simultaneously improves long-range consistency and motion dynamics of base AR-VDMs, a trade-off that sink-based methods fail to balance.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Progressive Pseudo-Label Optimization for Point-Supervised Change Detection
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Point-supervised change detection (PS-CD) aims to identify pixel-level changes between bi-temporal images using only sparsely annotated points. Although point annotations substantially reduce labeling costs, their limited spatial coverage often results in incomplete and noisy pseudo-labels. To address this issue, we propose a two-stage framework that introduces SAM2 priors into PS-CD and progressively adapts them to the target task. In Stage I, SAM2 generates object-aware candidate masks from point annotations on the bi-temporal images, and a bi-temporal mask selection strategy is designed to convert generic segmentation responses into more reliable change pseudo-labels. Subsequently, a lightweight CNN refinement module with an uncertainty-aware loss is employed to improve boundary quality and local structural consistency. In Stage II, we construct a teacher-student self-training framework in which the teacher is updated by exponential moving average and periodically refreshes the pseudo-labels. This design establishes a closed-loop optimization process that alternates between pseudo-label refinement and model re-optimization. Experiments on three benchmark datasets, including WHU-CD, LEVIR-CD, and SYSU-CD, demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms previous weakly supervised approaches on most benchmarks and remains competitive with several fully supervised methods.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Learning a Flow to Self-Supervised Representations
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We introduce Flow-Based Distribution Matching (FBDM), which learns self-supervised representations through non-adversarial velocity regression. The encoder and auxiliary field are trained jointly by regressing analytic velocities along spherical paths from learned representations to reference targets. Both augmented views share a reference target, with a capacity limit on each reference center and an explicit view-alignment loss. A structured reference supports more components than the auxiliary flow dimension while retaining geometric separation. The auxiliary field is discarded after pretraining; only the backbone is retained downstream. On three ResNet-18 benchmarks with matched auxiliary parameter counts, FBDM provides 2.17 to 2.36 times higher per-epoch training throughput than critic-based Distribution Matching (DM), with about 0.21 GiB additional peak allocated GPU memory. Experiments show that FBDM is competitive with existing SSL methods from CIFAR to ImageNet and performs comparably to DM on their shared benchmarks. Under stated conditions, our population analysis bounds nearest-centroid classification error on the initial normalized pretraining representation by the FBDM loss.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: OmniOPD: Stable On-Policy Distillation for Joint Audio-Video Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) elevates joint audio-video generation, but optimizing heterogeneous, modality-specific audio and video rewards often introduces cross-modal interference. On-policy distillation (OPD) alleviates this issue by transferring the capabilities of specialized audio and video RL teachers into a single student model. However, a significant imbalance in cross-modal token counts leaves audio with sparse supervision, causing unstable distillation. We observe that naively increasing the audio loss weight fails to solve this problem since audio learning relies heavily on visual context, indicating richer visual cues are crucial to offset sparse audio signals. To address this, we propose OmniOPD, a modality-wise on-policy distillation framework designed for balanced and stable audio-video generation. First, we construct privileged visual information using asymmetric noise scheduling, allowing the audio teacher to generate more informative targets from cleaner video context. Second, we introduce grouped multi-noise sampling to expand audio supervision coverage and stabilize training. Third, we introduce timestep-wise importance weighting based on teacher-student transition divergence, preserving reliable supervision while down-weighting unreliable learning signals, to stabilize fluctuations in audio learning. Evaluated on JavisBench and VBench demonstrate OmniOPD preserves audio quality while significantly enhancing video generation, achieving effective joint distillation.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Local-Global Joint Modeling for Point Cloud Super-Resolution Guided by Multi-Scale Spatial Priors
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Range-image-based point cloud super-resolution provides an effective way to reconstruct sparse outdoor point clouds by projecting low-resolution LiDAR scans into a regular 2D representation. However, current methods still face three challenges. First, range images exhibit pronounced vertical nonuniformity, with sparse observations in distant regions and denser observations in nearby regions. Some cross-scale fusion mechanisms do not account for the varying reliability of features at different vertical positions, allowing invalid values and noise from distant sparse regions to propagate into the decoder. Second, a single convolutional or sequence-modeling architecture often struggles to preserve both local high-frequency geometric details and global long-range dependencies, resulting in over-smoothed reconstructions. Third, smooth transition depths near foreground-background boundaries can produce spike artifacts when the 2D range image is back-projected into 3D. To address these issues, we propose a point cloud super-resolution method based on multi-scale spatial priors and joint local-global modeling. The design comprises a spatially gated fusion module, a multi-granularity local-global cooperative perception module, and 2D median-residual denoising. Experiments on KITTI-360 and nuScenes demonstrate effective reconstruction, with IoU scores of 0.4703 and 0.3593, respectively, supporting the feasibility of the proposed method for range-image super-resolution.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Deep learning-based self-supervised detection and localization of magnetic resonance imaging anomalies in artificial intelligence-supported radiotherapy workflows
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into radiotherapy workflows, yet it remains vulnerable to out-of-distribution image data that can introduce unexpected behavior in clinical tasks. Deep learning (DL)-based anomaly detection for pelvic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains limited and transparent evaluation for full automation is lacking. This study aimed to develop two self-supervised anomaly-detection framework variations in radiotherapy for pelvic and brain MRI.A two-stage self-supervised DL-framework was trained separately for pelvic and brain MRI utilizing three public datasets. The first stage compressed normal image data into discrete representations, and a second stage modeled the representation distribution. Anomaly-evidence was obtained by combining perceptual image differences with token-surprisal scores via negative log-likelihood estimation. Automated detection was evaluated for two anatomical cohorts: pelvis, encompassing both synthetic global anomalies and real clinical anomalies, and brain, comprising clinically annotated anomalies. Performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). For each cohort, a subset of normal images was reserved for analysis. Promising exploratory performance across evaluation cohorts was obtained. AUCs were 0.97 (95% CI 0.96-0.99) for synthetic pelvic anomalies, 0.95 (95% CI 0.90-1.00) for clinical pelvic anomalies, and 0.81 (95% CI 0.74-0.87) for brain anomalies. Qualitative heatmap analysis showed spatial agreement between detected anomalies and reference annotations. The framework variations showed promising anomaly detection performance across pelvic and brain MRI, supporting its potential for automated MRI quality control in radiotherapy. Heatmap-based visualization further improved interpretability by spatially localizing detected anomalies.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: This paper has been published in Physics and Imaging in Radiation Oncology (phiRO)

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Material-informed Gaussian Splatting for 3D World Reconstruction in a Digital Twin
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: 3D reconstruction for Digital Twins often relies on LiDAR-based methods, which provide accurate geometry but lack the semantics and textures naturally captured by cameras. Traditional LiDAR-camera fusion approaches require complex calibration and still struggle with certain materials like glass, which are visible in images but poorly represented in point clouds. We propose a camera-only pipeline that reconstructs scenes using 3D Gaussian Splatting from multi-view images, extracts semantic material masks via vision models, converts Gaussian representations to mesh surfaces with projected material labels, and assigns physics-based material properties for accurate sensor simulation in modern graphics engines and simulators. This approach combines photorealistic reconstruction with physics-based material assignment, providing sensor simulation fidelity comparable to LiDAR-camera fusion while eliminating hardware complexity and calibration requirements. We validate our camera-only method using an internal dataset from an instrumented test vehicle, leveraging LiDAR as ground truth for reflectivity validation alongside image similarity metrics.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Accepted to IEEE Intelligent Vehicles Symposium (IV) 2026. Revised version (v4) presents camera-ready publication

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: History Forcing: Distilling History-Dependent Continuations for Long-Horizon Video World Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Few-step autoregressive video diffusion enables efficient generation, yet maintaining consistency over long rollouts remains challenging, especially when subjects or scenes reappear after going out of sight. Despite progress in fidelity and rollout robustness, existing distillation methods do not fully exploit richer historical information to constrain the student's current prediction. To address this gap, we introduce \textbf{History Forcing}, a unified on-policy distillation framework that strengthens historical supervision for few-step autoregressive video generators. The framework uses the residual between teacher predictions with and without informative historical context to decouple this supervision. Such a historical context can be obtained using earlier generated chunks with less accumulated drift or a fixed-view teacher rollout that keeps the scene visible while the student looks away. The residual is then weighted and added to the score or velocity prediction used for distillation, forming a corrected target. By aligning the student with this corrected target through distillation, History Forcing incorporates long-range historical constraints into autoregressive generation. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance among 1.3B models, with a VBench quality score of 85.07 for 15s video generation and a VBench-Long aggregate score of 79.82 for 60s generation. For out-of-sight world modeling, evaluations further demonstrate more plausible scene evolution and more consistent states when the camera returns, with Evolution Quality improving from 2.35 to 2.70 on PlayWorld and Object Consistency from 58.43 to 62.18 on MemoBench.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Lookahead Prediction-Guided Adaptive Visual Refocusing for Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Interleaved multimodal chain-of-thought reasoning improves the visual reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models by dynamically incorporating visual evidence during reasoning. However, existing methods primarily select evidence from historical context. When the reasoning focus shifts, history-guided evidence may remain focused on prior regions and fail to cover the visual information required by the next step. We refer to this lag between visual evidence and subsequent reasoning demands as Temporal Evidence Myopia. To address this issue, we propose Lookahead Prediction-guided Adaptive Visual Refocusing (LPAVR), a training-free test-time framework. LPAVR transforms Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) from a decoding acceleration mechanism into a lookahead signal for anticipating upcoming reasoning intent. During MTP decoding, the draft head generates multiple future tokens, while the target model verifies them in parallel and retains the longest prefix consistent with its decoding trajectory. This target-verified prefix contains near-future semantics, which LPAVR uses to construct lookahead-guided visual evidence and assess whether history-guided evidence covers the indicated regions. If the coverage is sufficient, the history-guided evidence is retained; otherwise, LPAVR switches to the lookahead-guided evidence. This better aligns the visual context with upcoming reasoning and improves consistency between draft predictions and target-model decoding. Experiments on multiple multimodal reasoning benchmarks show that LPAVR improves both reasoning accuracy and the acceptance rates of MTP speculative tokens, jointly enhancing visual reasoning and speculative decoding efficiency.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: LipLingo: CNN Model for Lip Reading
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Lip reading plays a crucial role in applications such as speech recognition, assistive technologies for the hearing-impaired, and biometric authentication. However, performance often degrades when the speaker varies and when certain speech sounds are visually similar. To address these challenges, we propose LipLingo, a robust lip-reading system based on the LipNet architecture, enhanced with a standardized preprocessing pipeline for consistent mouth-region representation, a rotational validation strategy for improved generalization to unseen speakers, and a flexible similarity evaluation for more reliable sentence-level assessment. The model architecture combines 3D convolutional layers for spatio-temporal feature extraction and bidirectional recurrent layers for sequence modeling, optimized using the Adam optimizer and Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) loss. On the GRID dataset, LipLingo achieved 95.0\% character-level accuracy (CER 4.99\%) and 87.2\% sentence-level accuracy. At the corpus level, the system obtained a (WER 13.1\%), outperforming the baseline LipNet and demonstrating competitive performance relative to recent 3D-ResNet + Bi-GRU + MixUp approaches. These results provide insights into strategies that enhance lip-reading robustness and highlight directions for future work toward real-world deployment.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Risk-Constrained Evaluation of Financial Document Recognition: A Formal Framework for Evidence, Critical Errors, and Selective Automation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Financial document recognition is commonly evaluated using character and word error rates, which do not adequately represent the consequences of errors in financial workflows. This paper formalizes financial document recognition as a risk-constrained evidence-recovery problem. It defines typed, evidence-linked financial facts and a multi-layer quality model spanning text, layout, tables, fields, semantic relations, calibration, robustness, and operational performance. It introduces non-compensatory acceptance gates based on upper confidence bounds for critical-field errors, and formulates selective automation as a constrained risk-coverage problem with review-capacity limits. The paper also specifies annotation requirements, leakage-resistant benchmark splits, statistical estimands, and a reproducibility card. Formal propositions establish why aggregate scores cannot certify critical-field reliability and why zero observed errors do not imply zero risk. A synthetic example illustrates the decision rule. The work is theoretical; no empirical benchmark or model performance claim is presented.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Unlocking the Potential of Vision Foundation Models for Multi-Task Dense Prediction via Mixture of Task Adapters
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Multi-task dense prediction seeks a single, coherent representation that supports simultaneously discriminative semantic recognition and regularized geometric/structural inference. For vision foundation models, pretrained semantic invariances conflict with the frequency and smoothness biases of dense objectives; joint fine-tuning and single-route adapters therefore compress competing gradients into one update channel, causing negative transfer and unstable cross-task agreement. We frame this as two-level adaptation: task-generic alignment that preserves priors, and task-aware specialization that resolves late-stage conflicts. Based on this principle, we propose D2MoE , a Mixture of Task Adapters that explicitly factorizes these roles within a frozen DINOv3 backbone. D2MoE introduces Task-Generic Low-Rank Adaptation (TG-LoRA) in attention projections throughout the network to provide a stable, shared adaptation channel, and a Task-Adaptive Mixture of Experts (TA-MoE) injected only at the final attention block of each stage to enact sparse, task-conditioned perturbations of token mixing in a single forward pass. A Semantic Prior Injector further couples multi-level task features with frozen foundation priors to reinforce semantic coherence while preserving boundary and structural fidelity. Experiments across diverse benchmarks substantiate that this structured factorization yields robust multi-task improvements with a small trainable footprint, establishing a principled and scalable route to prior-preserving, foundation-centric multi-task dense perception.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: GaussFlaw: Fine-Grained Perceptual Diagnosis for 3D Gaussian Splatting
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables photorealistic novel- view synthesis with real-time rendering, yet fine-grained di- agnosis of its rendering artifacts remains challenging. These artifacts are typically spatially localized and exhibit diverse degradation patterns, making them difficult to character- ize using global quality metrics and image-level assessment benchmarks, which provide no explicit indication of where they occur or what types of artifacts they represent. To ad- dress this limitation, we introduce GaussFlaw-80K, the first large-scale dataset for fine-grained perceptual diagnosis in 3DGS. Constructed through a model-assisted human-in-the- loop pipeline, GaussFlaw-80K contains 80,049 artifact re- gions across 14,289 rendered images, each annotated with a pixel-level mask and one of eight flaw labels spanning ge- ometric, blending, and photometric degradations. These an- notations turn 3DGS artifact diagnosis into an explicit and measurable task. Building on this dataset, we propose Ge- oCritic, a geometry-guided multi-task model that integrates RGB appearance with depth-derived cues to jointly localize artifacts and classify their flaw types. Beyond evaluation, we further demonstrate the downstream benefits of fine-grained diagnosis through three complementary targeted operations: Gaussian densification, attribute correction, and outlier prun- ing. Experiments show that GeoCritic achieves an AUC-J of 0.9507 and an Acc@1 of 80.08%, while diagnosis-guided re- finement improves all reported global and crop-level metrics across diverse datasets and 3DGS backbones.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: EV9V: An Echocardiographic Video Benchmark with Uncertainty Guided View Classification
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Automated classification of standard echocardiographic views is crucial for efficient clinical workflow but faces three main challenges. First, publicly available datasets are scarce and limited in scale and view coverage. Second, the performance of some modern video-level architectures for echocardiographic view classification remains underexplored. Third, some view categories exhibit highly similar spatial appearances, making single-frame features insufficient for discrimination, while heterogeneous frame quality complicates robust temporal information fusion. To address these challenges, we release the Echocardiographic Videos of Nine Views (EV9V) dataset, comprising 5,138 videos, 910,579 frames, and 9 standard views, which is, to the best of our knowledge, the largest openly released echocardiography video dataset. Furthermore, we propose a Spatio-Temporal Fusion Model (STFM), an efficient dual-stream framework that jointly captures spatial anatomical structures and temporal cardiac dynamics. The STFM leverages uncertainty-aware learning to preferentially sample representative video segments during training and evidence-based fusion during inference, improving robustness to variations in frame quality across echocardiographic videos. Extensive experiments demonstrate that STFM achieves competitive performance and effectiveness compared with diverse video classification architectures, including two-dimensional and three-dimensional convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, and Transformers. The code is released at https://huggingface.co/datasets/bgx666/EV9V and the EV9V dataset is available at https://github.com/bgx666/stfm.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Trace4D: Grounded Spatiotemporal Reasoning via 4D State Sequences
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Understanding how objects and their spatial relationships evolve in 3D space over time remains challenging for vision-language models (VLMs), particularly under changing viewpoints. Recent approaches incorporate geometric information into reasoning, but explicit supervision for temporally ordered 4D state evolution and its use as intermediate evidence remains limited. We introduce \textbf{Trace4D}, which trains VLMs to predict 4D state sequences and reason over their inter-timestep changes alongside temporal visual observations. Its 4D-grounded chain-of-thought (CoT) explicitly represents 4D states, analyzes temporal visual context, and connects both as evidence for the answer. We construct Trace4D-Train from in-the-wild videos with 600K 4D perception examples and approximately 70K grounded QA examples, and train with joint supervised fine-tuning followed by geometry-aware GRPO. At inference, Trace4D predicts 4D states and reasoning directly from video without reference annotations or an external geometric model. Experiments on Trace4D-Bench and VLM4D show improved QA accuracy over the base VLMs and benefits from reasoning over 4D state changes and temporal visual observations.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: DINOFAS: Bonafide-Centric Representation Learning for Face Anti-Spoofing
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Face anti-spoofing (FAS) models often learn attack- and dataset-specific cues that degrade performance under unseen acquisition conditions and presentation attacks. We present DINOFAS, a DINOv3-based framework that formulates FAS as bonafide-centric representation learning. The proposed framework combines parameter-efficient DINOv3 adaptation using low-rank adaptation (LoRA), an attention style-content disentanglement (ASCD) module for reducing domain-specific appearance variations, and a dual-branch architecture that separates prototype-based liveness learning from attack-semantic supervision. The model is jointly optimized using a bonafide-centric prototype objective, an attack-semantic classification loss applied to detached features, and orthogonality regularization. DINOFAS achieves an average HTER of 9.09\% under the standard OCIM leave-one-domain-out protocol, where training is performed on three source datasets and evaluation is conducted on the held-out unseen domain. We further evaluate synthetic-to-real generalization by training exclusively on SynthASpoof and testing on four unseen real-world datasets, where DINOFAS achieves the lowest average HTER of 21.41\% and the highest average AUC of 86.14\% among the compared methods. Evaluations on OULU-NPU and SiW-Mv2 additionally demonstrate robustness to variations in acquisition conditions, devices, and unseen presentation attacks.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Pair-Relative Partial Equivariance for Rotation-Robust Keypoint Descriptor Matching
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Learned keypoint descriptors trained on upright imagery often fail under large in-plane rotation. Steerers address this by applying a single exact SO(2) representation to the descriptor space, but this global group constraint can be too rigid for keypoint descriptors, whose angular responses need not follow a single group representation. We propose pair-relative partial equivariance, which measures equivariance under the empirical distribution of relative rotations in image pairs, and PaSteer, a relaxed descriptor-steering framework that allows the steering map to leave the exact representation manifold while retaining the lightweight, backbone-free design of steering. PaSteer instantiates this relaxation with two variants: an identity-preserving residual steerer (PaSteer-soft) and a free-form Fourier steerer (PaSteer-free). We show that the per-angle optimal linear steerer for a fixed non-equivariant descriptor generally does not obey the group composition law, explaining why exact representations can be suboptimal in the frozen-descriptor regime. On Roto-360, MegaDepth-1500, AIMS, and IMC-PT, PaSteer consistently improves rotation-robust matching over an exact steerer on frozen DeDoDe descriptors, especially under large relative rotations, with minimal upright degradation.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Spatial-Frequency-Aware Implicit Neural Representation of Multidimensional Signals via MLP-KAN Fusion
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) have emerged as a compelling paradigm for modeling multidimensional signals by mapping continuous coordinates to signal values. However, Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLP)-based INRs inherently suffer from spectral bias, which favors low-frequency components and suppresses the reconstruction of essential high-frequency details. While existing techniques, such as Fourier feature mappings, mitigate this issue, they often rely on sensitive manual tuning and are prone to spectral artifacts. In this paper, we propose a spatial-frequency-aware INR framework that combines an MLP branch with a Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KAN) branch for complementary frequency-oriented modeling. The MLP branch provides a low-frequency-oriented representation of smooth structures, whereas the KAN branch complements localized variations and fine details. To coordinate the two branches, we integrate the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and inverse discrete wavelet transform (IDWT) into the output fusion stage. The outputs of the two branches are decomposed into wavelet coefficients, and the corresponding coefficients are additively fused before inverse wavelet reconstruction. A wavelet-domain band-separation regularization further penalizes high-frequency responses in the MLP branch and low-frequency responses in the KAN branch, thereby encouraging complementary frequency-oriented behavior. Experiments on 1D signals, 2D images, 3D volumes and signed distance functions, videos, and 4D light-fields demonstrate the applicability of the proposed representation across the evaluated signal modalities. Results demonstrate improved reconstruction fidelity across the evaluated signal modalities.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: MOPDA: Mixed-Trajectory On-Policy Distillation for Language-Guided Industrial Anomaly Detection
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) have shown strong potential for industrial anomaly detection (IAD) by providing image-level anomaly judgments and interpretable reasoning. However, reliably translating generated judgments into precise pixel-level localization remains challenging. We propose \textbf{M}ixed-Trajectory \textbf{O}n-\textbf{P}olicy \textbf{D}istillation for Language-Guided Industrial \textbf{A}nomaly Detection (MOPDA), the first framework to introduce on-policy self-distillation into LVLM-based IAD. For judgment learning, \method introduces \textbf{Mixed-Trajectory Supervision}, combining student-generated on-policy trajectories with evidence-conditioned teacher trajectories under a shared token-level distillation objective. Student trajectories preserve supervision on deployment-relevant response paths, while teacher trajectories provide complementary evidence-conditioned supervision. For dense localization, \textbf{Language-guided Visual Anchoring} uses the final judgment as a compact semantic condition to construct image-specific normal and abnormal anchors, which are contrasted with dense visual features to produce anomaly maps. This keeps language as semantic guidance while grounding pixel-level responses in visual evidence. Under a strict cross-dataset zero-shot protocol on five IAD benchmarks, \method outperforms the evaluated LVLM-based baselines on most detection, localization, and judgment metrics while remaining competitive with CLIP-based methods. Ablations further validate both mixed-trajectory supervision and final-judgment conditioning.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Subspace Representations for Synthetic-to-Real Transfer in 3-D Surface Inspection
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: This paper studies what subspace representations contribute to synthetic-to-real transfer in 3-D surface inspection, where models learn from synthetic defects and the only real data before deployment are scans of good parts. We use three classical constructions as instruments: the nearest-subspace classifier, one-class template subspaces and the generalized difference subspace (GDS). On 1,197 MVTec 3D-AD scans without target annotation we find that every decision rule ranks real defects at a similar window AUC, that image-level detection stays at chance, and that no rule keeps its in-domain threshold. We show that the margin of a nearest-subspace rule moves by at most the part of the feature shift outside its class subspaces, and that this leakage, measured from unlabeled good scans, bounds the displacement observed on unseen scans. On 597 Real3D-AD objects, a one-class subspace of registered templates evaluated at every location on frozen features reaches point AUROC 0.957 on pre-registered scans and a category-mean object AUROC of 78 to 81 with no training on the benchmark. Our results suggest that a subspace helps under shift in proportion to the shift it spans, and that in reference-based inspection the reference and its registration matter more than the subspace.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 16 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables. Accepted to the ACCV 2026 Workshop on Subspaces in the Era of Foundation Models. Website: https://abdullah-nasir-chowdhury.github.io/projects/accv2026/

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: MoviEdit: Long-form Multi-Shot Video Editing Made Easy
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Long-form multi-shot video editing requires an intended edit to remain coherent across abrupt changes in scene, viewpoint, and subject appearance, while processing substantially longer visual context than conventional single-shot editors. We introduce MoviEdit, an end-to-end framework for scalable long-form multi-shot video editing that jointly addresses the challenges of data, modeling, and evaluation. To provide cross-shot supervision data at scale, we develop automatic data-generation pipelines spanning synchronized multi-view footage, real-world multi-shot videos, and generated multi-shot content, yielding 87K paired editing videos without manual annotation. Architecturally, MoviEdit employs a cascaded bidirectional-autoregressive design: a lightweight bidirectional stage first establishes a globally coherent editing draft over a spatiotemporally compressed representation, which is then autoregressively propagated and refined over the full video. We further introduce MoviEdit-Bench, a dedicated benchmark for systematic evaluation of long-form multi-shot video editing. Extensive experiments show that MoviEdit substantially outperforms existing open-source models and performs on par with industry frontier models across text-guided and image-guided editing. Visit our project page for complete results and to access the benchmark: https://multi-shot-edit.github.io/

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Attention Residual U-Net for Enhanced Cross-Dataset Polyp Localization in Endoscopy
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Precise localization of pathologies in endoscopy is a critical task in medical imaging, with deep learning (DL) frameworks now serving as the primary methodology for automated lesion detection. Today, generic object detection methods, such as YOLO, provide state-of-the-art performance in this context. However, their robustness often decreases under real-world clinical conditions due to variations across endoscopic devices, intestinal content, dataset bias, and the presence of small or low-contrast lesions. Motivated by these challenges, we propose a novel polyp detection framework based on a Attention Residual U-Net offering enhanced polyp localization. Instead of directly regressing bounding boxes from global feature representations, the proposed method learns lesion-focused spatial representations and converts them into bounding-box predictions during inference. Unlike conventional encoder-decoder localization frameworks that directly propagate all encoder activations into the decoding pathway, the proposed method selectively suppresses irrelevant background responses before feature reconstruction. This encourages the network to focus on lesion-relevant spatial evidence under heterogeneous imaging conditions. To achieve this, the framework integrates residual feature propagation, attention-guided encoder filtering, and multi-scale contextual learning. The proposed framework was evaluated on multiple public endoscopic datasets acquired using different devices. The comparative experimental results validate its effectiveness over the relevant state-of-the-art methods, with an improvement up to 22.0% in terms of the area under the receiving operating characteristic (AUC).

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: TACO: Trajectory-Aware Curvature Observation for Memorization Localization and Mitigation in Diffusion Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Text-to-image diffusion models can reproduce memorized training content within localized image regions, making precise localization essential for targeted mitigation. However, curvature observations at a single denoising state can contain transient responses, while spatially uniform mitigation may disrupt prompt-relevant content. We present Trajectory-Aware Curvature Observation (TACO), a unified framework for local memorization detection and mitigation in diffusion models. Our empirical analysis reveals that memorization-related curvature becomes pronounced during late-stage denoising and persists at consistent spatial locations across neighboring states. Motivated by these observations, TACO aggregates prompt-dependent curvature responses along the late denoising trajectory and applies latent-guided spatial refinement to improve spatial coherence. The resulting memorization map serves both as a localization signal and as a spatial control signal for mitigation. Specifically, TACO uses this map to steer existing inference-time interventions toward memorization-related regions through spatial reweighting and localized guidance correction. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TACO consistently outperforms competing localization methods and improves the Pareto trade-off between memorization suppression and generation quality. These results establish trajectory-aware spatial analysis as an effective link between memorization localization and targeted mitigation.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: DiffCap-Bench: A Comprehensive, Challenging, Robust Benchmark for Image Difference Captioning
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Image Difference Captioning (IDC) generates natural language descriptions that precisely identify differences between two images, serving as a key benchmark for fine-grained change perception, cross-modal reasoning, and image editing data construction. However, existing benchmarks lack diversity and compositional complexity, and standard lexical-overlap metrics (e.g., BLEU, METEOR) fail to capture semantic consistency or penalize hallucinations, which together prevent a comprehensive and robust evaluation of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on IDC. To address these gaps, we introduce DiffCap-Bench, a comprehensive IDC benchmark covering ten distinct difference categories to ensure diversity and compositional complexity. Furthermore, we propose an LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation protocol grounded in human-validated Difference Lists, enabling a robust assessment of models' ability to both capture and describe visual changes. Through extensive evaluation of state-of-the-art MLLMs, we reveal significant performance gaps between proprietary and open-source models, highlight the critical importance of reasoning capability, and identify clear limitations in model scaling. Our framework also demonstrates strong alignment with human expert judgments and strong correlation with downstream image editing data construction quality. These findings establish DiffCap-Bench as both a reliable IDC evaluation framework and a practical predictor of downstream utility. The benchmark and code will be made publicly available to support further research.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: 3L-D: A Low-Light Level Dataset from a Sensor-Agnostic, Alignment-Preserving Acquisition Framework
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Supervised low-light image and video enhancement has achieved remarkable progress, yet current models remain fundamentally constrained by the limitations of existing datasets. Prevailing methods typically rely on uncontrolled ambient captures, camera parameter manipulation (e.g., exposure or ISO adjustments), or neutral density filters, failing to replicate authentic night-sky near-infrared spectral content and genuine low-photon noise distributions. Furthermore, capturing dynamic paired sequences without introducing warping artifacts or sensor-specific biases remains an open challenge. In this paper, we introduce 3L-Dataset, a physically calibrated low-light image and video dataset generated using a modular, sensor-agnostic acquisition framework. Our test bench faithfully reproduces the standardized Midavaine night level scale from Level 1 (full moon, approximately 1000 mlx) down to Level 5 (overcast moonless night, approximately 0.1 mlx), spanning the visible to near-infrared spectrum across diverse realistic environments, including countryside, forest, urban, and desert scale models. Using high-precision programmable mechanical actuation, our acquisition framework guarantees sub-pixel spatial alignment across synchronized sextuplets, each composed of one reference image and five corresponding images acquired at the five standardized night levels, without post-processing image warping. We evaluate multiple representative deep learning baselines across varying night levels, revealing critical trade-offs between reconstruction fidelity, perceptual quality, and inference latency under severe photon starvation. The modular acquisition framework can be adapted to different cameras, optical systems, sensor technologies, and resolutions, enabling the dataset to be continuously expanded.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Efficient Cross-Scale Invertible Hiding Network with Spatial-Frequency Collaboration and Non-Invertible Mechanism
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Image hiding aims to conceal image-level messages within cover images at the same resolution. Invertible neural networks (INN)-based image hiding has emerged as an important branch. It treats concealing and revealing as a pair of inverse problems on image domain transformation and uses INN's forward and backward processes to address them. Due to architectural constraints, existing INN-based methods suffer from single-scale and single-domain feature extraction and limited nonlinear representation capability, resulting in inferior image quality. To mitigate these limitations, we propose an efficient cross-scale invertible hiding network with the spatial-frequency collaboration and the non-invertible mechanism, termed CrosInv. CrosInv exploits cross-scale and spatial-frequency collaborative features while enhancing nonlinear representation. Specifically, we introduce a cross-scale invertible module that bijectively maps inputs to cross-scale representations. To effectively integrate spatial and frequency information, the cross-scale invertible module employs pixel shuffle, Haar wavelet transformation, and their inverse operations for scale transformation. Furthermore, a non-invertible cross dense module is integrated to enhance the nonlinearity. Comprehensive experiments verify the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed CrosInv.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Submitted by Junxue Yang, Xin Liao (https://msf-hnu.github.io/)

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Human-Oriented World Model
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Supporting a person over repeated interactions requires interpreting their current state in context and anticipating its subsequent evolution. We formulate the \emph{Human-Oriented World Model} (HOWM) as a conceptual framework centered on task-relevant human states and their evolution. HOWM connects current observations and individual history with environmental and social context to organize continuing state estimation, personalized dynamics prediction, and action support. Dynamic expectations and new observations jointly inform the current estimate, which in turn anchors personalized forecasts based on shared knowledge and individual experience. An external policy relates forecasts under alternative conditions to the person's goals, preferences, and constraints when considering support. Actual responses and outcomes provide evidence for revising the state estimate and personal dynamic patterns, thereby informing subsequent estimation, prediction, and support. We illustrate the framework through hypothetical training and learning scenarios. Our research agenda asks whether accumulated interaction experience improves subsequent estimation and prediction, and whether using the model helps the person pursue their goals over time.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Discovering Semantic Granularity in Images through Clustering of Pretrained Visual Representations
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Semantic granularity, which refers to the levels at which visual representations organize image content into meaningful entities, is fundamental to image understanding. However, whether pretrained visual representations inherently encode semantic structures at multiple granularities remains poorly understood. This paper presents a representation-driven approach for discovering semantically meaningful image regions at different granularities through clustering of pretrained visual representations without semantic supervision. Specifically, we concatenate selected feature maps extracted from a pretrained visual model and apply a singular value decomposition (SVD)-based projection to derive pixel-wise principal representation maps (PRMs). The resulting PRMs capture implicit semantic structures embedded in pretrained visual representations, making them accessible to subsequent semantic clustering. We then introduce the semantic continuity rate (SCR), based on the silhouette principle, to quantify the coherence of pixel-wise representations within and between clusters at different candidate granularities. Furthermore, we analyze the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of SCR profiles to assess representation suitability for discovering semantic regions at multiple granularities. Our results indicate that PRMs exhibiting higher SNR values over an initial range of cluster numbers tend to yield more semantically meaningful regions across multiple granularities. We evaluate the proposed approach on the COCO-2017 and VOC-2012 validation datasets using Hungarian-matched intersection over union (HIoU). The results demonstrate competitive segmentation performance among the compared methods, supporting the feasibility of discovering useful semantic granularities through clustering PRMs without semantic supervision.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Geometry-Constrained Dynamic Hypergraph Convolutional Network with Contrastive Score Refinement for Skeleton-Based Action Recognition
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Skeleton-based action recognition is a pivotal task in computer vision; however, conventional Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) are often constrained by pairwise joint modeling, which fails to capture the intricate high-order interactions inherent in human movement. While recent hypergraph-based methods attempt to address this limitation, they typically rely on static structures derived from anatomical priors, lacking the flexibility to capture dynamic, action-specific joint correlations. To this end, we propose DyGCN, a Geometry-Constrained Dynamic Hypergraph Convolutional Network for skeleton-based action recognition. At the core of DyGCN is the Dynamic Hypergraph Construction Network with Contrastive Score Refinement (DyGCT) block, which comprises two novel components: the Geometry-Constrained Dynamic Hypergraph Construction (GeoHC) module and the Contrastive Score Refinement (CSR) module. Specifically, GeoHC dynamically constructs action-specific hyperedges by leveraging geometry-constrained second-order compatibility, transcending the limitations of static hyperedge structures. Furthermore, CSR explicitly refines the pairwise compatibility scores during hypergraph construction through prototype-based contrastive learning, fostering more discriminative action-specific hyperedges, with zero inference-time overhead as CSR operates only during training. Extensive experiments on NTU RGB+D, NTU RGB+D 120, and Northwestern-UCLA validate the effectiveness of DyGCN, achieving state-of-the-art performance on widely used benchmarks. The source code is available at https://github.com/marvineta0405/DyGCN.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: TME-ContextNet: Class-Conditioned Spatial Supervision and Grouped Decoding for Joint Nuclei Instance Segmentation and Classification
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Joint nuclei instance segmentation and classification requires precise boundaries and neighborhood information that helps distinguish morphologically similar cell types. We present TME-ContextNet, a multi-task framework that learns class-conditioned spatial context from existing nuclear annotations and organizes decoding into geometry-related and semantic task groups. Class-conditioned spatial supervision extends nuclear labels into a dense target using Euclidean distance transforms, requiring no additional tissue-region annotation. We derive its nearest-region interpretation and characterize its stability to small annotation perturbations. A local--global context module combines dilated convolution and self-attention, while a grouped task decoder reduces redundant computation. The spatial head supplies training supervision and is omitted during inference. Experiments on PanMix, CoNSeP, and PanNuke yield Dice scores of 80.23%, 65.32%, and 79.13%, and mean multi-class panoptic quality (mPQ+) scores of 67.62%, 35.50%, and 43.74%, respectively. PanNuke results are averaged across three test folds. Target and decoder controls support the combination of distance-based supervision and grouped decoding while identifying their dependence on task configuration. The framework uses 36.40 million parameters, compared with 54.74 million for HoVer-Net. These findings support a compact, context-aware formulation for joint nuclei analysis in computational pathology.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: PhysOmni: Physics-Grounded Multi-Object Scene Generation from a Single Image with Real-Time Interaction
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Recent generative video models achieve impressive visual quality but remain constrained by limited physical consistency and controllability. Existing video generation methods provide minimal physical control, and single-image-to-3D conversion approaches often suffer from object interpenetration. Furthermore, physics-based scene-level 3D generation methods exhibit spatial misalignment, stylized artifacts, and inconsistencies with the input data, restricting their use in realistic interactive video synthesis. We propose PhysOmni, a training-free framework that converts a single image into a physically consistent and controllable video through holistic scene-level 3D reconstruction. By rep?resenting the full scene geometry in a unified spatial coordinate system, PhysOmni resolves object penetration and alignment ambiguity. Unlike prior methods, this formulation enables accurate scene?level multi-object interactions and introduces richer, complex control types for advanced mechanics?based manipulation. By decoupling simulation from rendering, PhysOmni bypasses latency-heavy priors, achieving real-time physical interaction previews paired while preserving photorealistic visual fidelity. Experimental results demonstrate that PhysOmni substantially outperforms prior methods in physical fidelity, spatial coherence, and controllability. Project Page: https://zephipage.github.io/PhysOmni/

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: PriCBMs: Multi-granular Concept Bottleneck Vision-Language Models for Visual Privacy Recognition
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Widespread image sharing on social media has increased the need for visual privacy recognition to identify inadvertently exposed privacy information. However, multi-label visual privacy recognition presents two challenges. First, privacy categories represent high-level semantic attributes and do not have a one-to-one correspondence with visual objects. Different visual objects may involve the same privacy category, while the same type of object may contain different types of privacy-sensitive information. In this setting, direct prediction methods generally lack explicit guidance for identifying category-relevant privacy cues, leaving this process implicit in the learned image-to-label mapping and potentially limiting classification performance. Second, privacy cues are often distributed across image regions and may not be adequately represented by whole-image features. To address these challenges, we propose Privacy Concept Bottleneck Models (PriCBMs). By introducing privacy-related concepts as intermediate semantic representations, PriCBMs first identify category-relevant privacy cues through visual-concept matching and then predict privacy categories based on concept responses. This process makes privacy predictions more interpretable. To improve the quality of these concepts, we design a concept selection strategy based on target-category relevance, cross-category discriminability, and semantic diversity. Meanwhile, we introduce a global-region modeling module to capture localized privacy evidence while retaining global context. Experiments on VISPR and FineViP show that PriCBMs outperform evaluated competitors across all four multi-label metrics. Ablation studies and concept-quality analyses support the effectiveness of the proposed design. Code is available at https://github.com/sun2293674491-dotcom/PriCBMs.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: CoEnv: Code-Driven Exploration in Real-to-Sim Digital Twins for Multi-Arm Manipulation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: General-purpose coding agents can now write, debug, and refine entire robot programs, but only if they have somewhere to practice. Physical hardware is a poor practice ground: exploratory rollouts are slow to reset and, when several arms share a workspace, unsafe. Generic simulation benchmarks are safe but do not match the geometry, assets, or viewpoints of the workspace where the robot must actually work. We present CoEx (Code-driven Exploration), which lets the agent practice in an executable digital twin of its own deployment workspace. The twin is built by CoEnv, our real-to-sim framework, which reconstructs the physical scene from multi-view RGBD into a physics simulation. Inside it, a centralized code agent explores at the program level, writing a complete multi-arm program, running it in the twin, and refining it against grounded verification (privileged state checks, checkpoint predicates on risky steps, and adaptive viewpoints against inter-arm occlusion). Verified programs transfer to hardware through collision-checked deployment. On five real-world multi-arm tasks with up to three heterogeneous robots, CoEx reaches 70% average success, against 50% for the same system without the code agent (where a VLM must choose every primitive step by step), outperforms two prior VLM-planning frameworks, and produces verified episodes at 3.8-11.7x the ablated rate. Because every verified rollout is also a demonstration, exploration leaves reusable experience behind: a $π_{0.5}$ policy fine-tuned purely on 200 agent-generated rollouts reaches 100% and 70% real-robot success on two tasks, with no human demonstrations.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: v2: substantially revised, with a new title, framing, and experiments (v1 title: "CoEnv: Driving Embodied Multi-Agent Collaboration via Compositional Environment"). 26 pages, 8 figures, 9 tables. Project page: https://faceong.github.io/CoEnv/

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Parametric CAD Bench v3: Evaluating Agentic Parametric CAD Authoring from Text and Engineering Drawings
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Producing an executable CAD script is not sufficient to establish that an agent has satisfied an engineering design request. Evaluation must also consider the resulting geometry, specified dimensions, and native CAD modeling history. We present Parametric CAD Bench v3, a 100-task benchmark comprising 30 text-to-CAD creation tasks, 30 text-to-CAD create-and-edit tasks, and 40 tasks that reconstruct mechanical parts from engineering drawings. Agents operate in a pinned FreeCAD environment and submit native CAD artifacts to a separate programmatic verifier. The primary metric is mean continuous task reward, combining geometry similarity and specification consistency rather than binary task success. A September 24, 2026 snapshot covers 13 model-agent systems; Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 achieves the highest overall point estimate, 61.03%, and an image-to-CAD mean reward of 84.66%. These measurements describe complete systems, not isolated model capabilities. We release versioned tasks, evaluation configurations, and inspectable result artifacts.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 31 pages, 12 figures, 11 tables. Benchmark: https://cadbench.ai/ ; tasks and leaderboard: https://hub.harborframework.com/datasets/gnucleus-ai/cad-bench/v3 ; scoring code: https://github.com/gNucleus-AI/freecad-validator

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: OctreeSplat: Hierarchical Octree-Guided Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has shown considerable potential for novel view synthesis (NVS) and 3D reconstruction. Feed-forward methods avoid costly per-scene optimization, but fixed image or spatial resolutions limit their ability to allocate primitives according to local complexity. We present OctreeSplat, a hierarchical octree-guided feed-forward Gaussian splatting. OctreeSplat extracts multi-view features and geometric priors from a frozen visual foundation model (VFM), constructs a hierarchical octree, and predicts densification scores. The resulting representation allocates Gaussian primitives at spatially varying densities according to local complexity. Stochastic solids volume rendering improves depth rendering, strengthens geometric supervision, and supports surface reconstruction. When camera parameters are available, an optional test-time optimization (TTO) module improves agreement between predicted and ground-truth parameters. Training updates only 76 million additional parameters and requires 35 GPU-hours. Experiments on Replica, TUM, Tanks and Temples, and DTU demonstrate competitive RGB view synthesis, depth synthesis, and surface reconstruction. OctreeSplat reduces the number of Gaussian primitives while maintaining high reconstruction quality.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: VerdictAD: Few-Shot Anomaly Detection via Decision-Guided Refinement
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Detecting defects in real-world industrial inspection often requires learning from only a few normal images per category. Recent few-shot anomaly detection methods have achieved strong performance by measuring feature differences between query images and normal references. However, visual differences do not always indicate genuine defects, as normal appearance variations can also produce high anomaly scores. Conversely, structural or logical anomalies may not produce strong local feature differences, making them difficult to detect. To address this limitation, we introduce VerdictAD, a training-free framework that refines existing anomaly detectors through visual decisions. Rather than replacing existing detectors, VerdictAD adopts a typed decision model to assess the query image and its local regions against a few normal references. By directly producing structured decision probabilities without text generation, the model provides complementary evidence for refining anomaly responses at different spatial scales. Building on this capability, we introduce two modules: Global Verdict Refinement (GVR) uses image-level decisions to refine the overall anomaly score, while Local Verdict Refinement (LVR) aggregates regional decisions to refine the anomaly map. Combined with a simple DINOv2-based detector, VerdictAD achieves competitive performance in one-shot and few-shot anomaly detection. More importantly, as a plug-and-play framework, it consistently improves existing anomaly detectors across MVTec AD, VisA, and MVTec LOCO AD, achieving strong results across one-shot and few-shot settings. Our code and experimental logs are publicly available at https://github.com/sgstq0811/VerdictAD-Jev-AD.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Preprint with 5 tables and 7 figures. Code and experimental logs available at https://github.com/sgstq0811/VerdictAD-Jev-AD

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Probe-Guided Gradient Balancing for Multimodal Learning
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Jointly trained multimodal networks frequently underutilize weaker modalities, as faster-learning modalities dominate the shared fusion objective and suppress gradients reaching slower ones. Most existing approaches throttle dominant modalities, whereas directly boosting weaker modalities often fails because monitoring signals derived from the joint loss remain dominated by stronger modalities. We propose Probe-Guided Gradient Boosting (PGGB), a gradient modulation approach that boosts weaker modalities while preserving the strength of dominant ones. PGGB attaches lightweight linear classifiers to stop-gradient features from each modality to estimate representation quality independently. The gap between these scores, termed the utilization gap, provides an imbalance signal used to adaptively scale weaker-modality gradients through bounded and smoothed modulation. PGGB is composable with throttling methods, as it leaves the loss function and fusion architecture unchanged. Experiments across eight benchmarks spanning four domains and 2-4 modalities demonstrate that PGGB outperforms state-of-the-art methods on highly imbalanced multimodal datasets while remaining competitive under low or negligible imbalance. We further establish bounded scaling, self-attenuation, and a descent bound for standard SGD under smoothness and bounded-variance assumptions. Code is available at https://github.com/VuVoCodes/PGGB.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Computer Vision Applications for Art History: Reflections and paradigms for future research
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: One of the contributing factors to the continuing debate among art historians over the use of computational methods in art history research is that they do not consider the core of today's art history research questions. The lack of close collaboration between the two involved research communities makes the definition of contemporary art-historical methods as well-defined computer vision problems extremely difficult. For that purpose, it is devised as a methodology to study articles in art history journals from a computer science perspective. The objective is to identify which image features art historians utilise within their research and describe them in immediate and meaningful terms to the computer vision research community. Finally, some paradigms that could serve as a new starting point for exploring how computer vision applications for art history can address the core of today's art history research are given.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 8 pages. Published in the Proceedings of EVA London 2021 (Electronic Visualisation and the Arts), BCS Electronic Workshops in Computing (eWiC), under CC BY 4.0

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: ReinSeg: Retrieval-Guided Bounded Multimodal Refinement for 3-D Road Anomaly Segmentation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: 3-D road anomaly segmentation is essential for risk-aware perception in autonomous driving. Its central challenge is to rank sparsely observed hazards ahead of abundant normal road structures while preserving point-wise metric localization.
